policy: Selected occupations and documented sieges, not a claim of exhaustive political history. Regional context is identified explicitly. Missing siege records never mean a site was never besieged.

Jerusalem.occupation: Frankish 1099–1187; Ayyubid 1187–1229; Frankish treaty possession 1229–1239 and 1241–1244; Khwarazmian capture 1244
Jerusalem.notes: The short 1239–1241 interruption is retained; treaty possession did not include every sacred precinct.

Jaffa.occupation: Frankish 1099–1187; restored 1191; intermittent Frankish possession to Mamluk conquest 1268
Jaffa.notes: Do not read the outer dates as uninterrupted Frankish control.

Caesarea.occupation: Frankish 1101–1187; restored 1191; later Frankish phases to Mamluk conquest 1265
Caesarea.notes: Intervening destruction and occupation require finer local phase review.

Bethlehem.occupation: Frankish 1099–1187; Ayyubid 1187–1229; Latin kingdom 1229–1244; Muslim rule after 1244

Nazareth.occupation: Frankish 1099–1187; restored by treaty 1229; sacked by Baybars 1263
Nazareth.notes: Selected phases; possession between individual agreements requires further local review.

Tiberias.occupation: Frankish city until 1187; Galilean territories restored 1240/1241; later local end date under review

Tartus.occupation: Templar citadel from 1152; citadel retained after attack in 1188; evacuated 1291

Alexandria.occupation: Egyptian dynastic context: Fatimid to 1171; Ayyubid 1171–1250; Mamluk 1250–1291 (continues)
Alexandria.notes: Regional political chronology, not continuous local garrison documentation. The 1365 raid is outside this map.

Mansoura.occupation: Founded during Fifth Crusade, 1219; Ayyubid then Mamluk Egyptian city; battle 1250 was not a lasting Frankish occupation

Mystras.occupation: Frankish castle founded 1249; Byzantine possession from 1262 to 1291 (continues)

Kozan.occupation: Sis: royal seat of Armenian Cilicia, kingdom established 1198; earlier local transitions under review

Paphos.occupation: Cypriot regional context: Byzantine until 1191; conquest 1191; Lusignan kingdom 1192–1291 (continues)
Paphos.notes: Regional sovereignty rather than a complete local garrison or monastic tenure history.

Larnaca.occupation: Cypriot regional context: Byzantine until 1191; conquest 1191; Lusignan kingdom 1192–1291 (continues)
Larnaca.notes: Regional sovereignty rather than a complete local garrison or monastic tenure history.

Kykkos.occupation: Cypriot regional context: Byzantine until 1191; conquest 1191; Lusignan kingdom 1192–1291 (continues)
Kykkos.notes: Regional sovereignty rather than a complete local garrison or monastic tenure history.

Bellapais.occupation: Cypriot regional context: Byzantine until 1191; conquest 1191; Lusignan kingdom 1192–1291 (continues)
Bellapais.notes: Regional sovereignty rather than a complete local garrison or monastic tenure history.

Mount Athos.occupation: Orthodox monastic community throughout 1095–1291; first charter 972
Mount Athos.notes: Religious community continuity; not a claim of a military occupation.

Patmos.occupation: Monastery of St John, founded 1088; Orthodox community during 1095–1291
Patmos.notes: Monastic presence, not a complete political-control history.

Rhodes.occupation: Byzantine/local rule; Leo Gabalas administration from 1204; Hospitaller occupation begins only after this map period

Damascus.occupation: Burid emirate in early 12th century; Zengid under Nur al-Din 1154–1174; later Ayyubid and Mamluk phases
Damascus.notes: Selected named phases; subsequent local transitions and brief Mongol occupation require a finer chronology.

Aleppo.occupation: Ayyubid 1183–1260; Mongol conquest 1260; earlier Zengid and later Mamluk phases

Nablus.notes: The Templar raid of 1242 was not a permanent return to Frankish occupation.

Mount Tabor.occupation: Benedictine/Frankish monastery until 1187; Ayyubid fortress begun 1212; later Christian/Hospitaller phases to 1263

Mount Carmel.occupation: Carmelite hermit community, early 13th century–1291; Rule received 1206–1214
Mount Carmel.notes: Religious presence is distinguished from sovereignty or a castle garrison.

Thessaloniki.occupation: Byzantine until 1204; Latin kingdom 1204–1224; Epirote rule 1224–1246; Nicaean/Byzantine from 1246 to 1291 (continues)
Thessaloniki.notes: Selected documented phases; not an exhaustive sequence of every local ruler or garrison.

Andravida.occupation: Frankish capital of Achaea from 1205 to 1291 (continues); earlier Byzantine settlement
Andravida.notes: Selected documented phases; not an exhaustive sequence of every local ruler or garrison.

Chalkida.occupation: Latin triarchs after 1204/1205; Venetian rights and shared rule from 1209 through 1291
Chalkida.notes: Selected documented phases; not an exhaustive sequence of every local ruler or garrison.

Monemvasia.occupation: Frankish capture conventionally 1248 (alternative 1252/1253); Byzantine again from 1262 to 1291 (continues)
Monemvasia.notes: Selected documented phases; not an exhaustive sequence of every local ruler or garrison.

Corfu.occupation: Angevin possession from 1267 to 1291 (continues); earlier Byzantine, Norman and Epirote phases
Corfu.notes: Selected documented phases; not an exhaustive sequence of every local ruler or garrison.

Zakynthos.occupation: Byzantine until 1185; Norman conquest and county palatine from 1185 through 1291
Zakynthos.notes: Selected documented phases; not an exhaustive sequence of every local ruler or garrison.

Gelibolu.occupation: Byzantine; Venetian interval 1204–1235; Byzantine again from 1235 through 1291
Gelibolu.notes: Selected documented phases; not an exhaustive sequence of every local ruler or garrison.

Mytilene.occupation: Byzantine island; Latin allocation from 1204; Byzantine reintegration by 1261 (selected phases)
Mytilene.notes: Selected documented phases; not an exhaustive sequence of every local ruler or garrison.

Izmir.occupation: Byzantine/Nicaean administrative centre in 12th–13th centuries; officials attested in 1207
Izmir.notes: Selected documented phases; not an exhaustive sequence of every local ruler or garrison.

Alasehir.occupation: Philadelphia: Byzantine/Nicaean administrative centre in 12th–13th centuries
Alasehir.notes: Selected documented phases; not an exhaustive sequence of every local ruler or garrison.

Sebastia.occupation: Frankish settlement and bishopric, 12th century–July 1187; taken by Saladin’s nephew in 1187

Gerasa.occupation: Damascene fort destroyed by Baldwin II in 1121; not established as a lasting Frankish garrison

Sidon.occupation: Frankish December 1110–July 1187; restored 1197–1291, with shared-control and interruption phases
Sidon.notes: Later condominium and short Muslim occupation phases require local dating; outer dates are not uninterrupted sole Frankish control.

Hama.occupation: Ayyubid principality from 1175 through 1291; Mamluk suzerainty in the later 13th century
Hama.notes: Selected attested phases; local succession between listed events is not represented as uninterrupted rule.

Homs.occupation: Ayyubid from late 12th century; Mamluk annexation 1262, continuing through 1291
Homs.notes: Selected attested phases; local succession between listed events is not represented as uninterrupted rule.

Baalbek.occupation: Zengi captured the citadel in 1139; Ayyubid emirate from 1175; Mongol capture 1260
Baalbek.notes: Selected attested phases; local succession between listed events is not represented as uninterrupted rule.

Shaizar.occupation: Banu Munqidh 1081–1157; Nur al-Din took control after the 1157 earthquake
Shaizar.notes: Selected attested phases; local succession between listed events is not represented as uninterrupted rule.

Bosra.occupation: Zengid governor confirmed 1154; Ayyubid city under al-Adil and successors, 1196–1260; Mongol capture 1260, then Mamluk rule
Bosra.notes: Selected dated holdings or transitions, not an exhaustive tenure list. Regional and construction evidence do not prove continuous local control.

Anavarza.occupation: Armenian capture 1111; Byzantine interlude 1137–1144; Armenian capital/fortress thereafter (selected phases)
Anavarza.notes: Selected dated holdings or transitions, not an exhaustive tenure list. Regional and construction evidence do not prove continuous local control.

Feke.occupation: Armenian capture in the 1090s from a Byzantine garrison; Byzantine recapture in John II’s campaign, 1137/1138
Feke.notes: Selected dated holdings or transitions, not an exhaustive tenure list. Regional and construction evidence do not prove continuous local control.
